contrast: CRYO vs PHE (both inert, 4 degC, 4 h)
prior_expectation: equivalent; Phase 0 bounds the gap at <=1.05 pp marker retention
decision: THE CAPITAL DECISION. Equivalence declared -> do not buy the cryo system; buy the PHE. Equivalence NOT declared AND CRYO superior on DA/hedonic -> cryo has a case.
THE OPERATIONAL DECISION. If significant, inert flush is mandatory kit regardless of which chiller is bought. Establishes that the panel is sensitive to the variable that actually matters.

prior_expectation: likely equivalent at 4 h; possible divergence at 8 h via longer warm-oxygen exposure
decision: Bounds the whole chilling-rate axis. If even passive cooling is equivalent, no chiller capital is justified at all.

prior_expectation: detectable difference neat (no native CO2, regenerated crema); possibly not in milk
decision: Quantifies the quality cost of batching at all. Sets the size of the gap the business must accept. Not a go/no-go on cryo.
PANEL VALIDITY GATE. If not significant at p<0.01, the panel/serving protocol is broken and NO other contrast may be interpreted. Analyse this first.

contrast: 4 h vs 8 h hold, within CRYO and within PHE
prior_expectation: degradation visible by 8 h; fines sediment by ~1.2 h
decision: Sets the service-window SOP. Constrained by safety to <=48 h at <=4 degC with HACCP regardless of sensory result.
